spec_match.rationale: Exercises the explainer's element surface (stream/enabled properties, permissionconstraints script child, streamready + userchangedenabled events), but event vocabulary conflicts with the sibling event-sequence concept which describes activate/error, and the element is unverifiable in this environment.

interactive.rationale: Real <usermedia> element plus mute/stop controls, live state grid and a timestamped event log — no static code-card (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card promises request/preview/mute-toggle/event-inspection and the page delivers exactly those panels.

edge_cases.rationale: Permission-denied (onerror + um.error) and stop/restart are handled, but there is no mid-session track-ended/device-unplug handling and no behind-a-flag enable path for browsers where the element is absent.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite runs live (4 pass / 2 fail here) and its negative branches are honest, but streamready-event-attribute is vacuous — setAttribute/hasAttribute passes in any browser for any element, so it proves nothing about the event handler slot (flagged for a human; suite is immutable).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): unsupported notice shows, controller card hides, conformance panel renders 4/2/0 — but the granted-stream path, mute toggle and events could not be exercised without the element or a camera. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: The server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js captures runtime/resource errors, but the page emits no custom interaction or assert events for the stream lifecycle it demonstrates.

design_system.rationale: All colours are design-system variables (including --accent-amber which exists in styles.css), and .ctrl-btn hover overrides background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons are native with labels and the clear control has role=button + keyboard handler, but the event log and state grid have no aria-live region, so stream/mute state changes are visual-only for screen readers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Layout uses flex-wrap and a 480px state-grid breakpoint and rendered without horizontal overflow at 1280px headless, but the narrow-mobile (≈360px, touch) class was not exercised in this cloud session.

openQuestions.title: Fix the stale version claim and add flag/enable steps to the unsupported banner
openQuestions.detail: The unsupported notice says '<usermedia> requires Chrome 149 or later', but the lineage note on the feature index records the element actually shipping in Chrome 151. In Chrome 149/150 the banner is therefore misleading. Per build rule 10, the banner should name the real requirement (Chrome 151, or the runtime-enabled-feature flag discovered via runtime_enabled_features.json5) with exact chrome://flags / --enable-features steps.

openQuestions.title: Hide or repurpose the event log when the element is unsupported
openQuestions.detail: When HTMLUserMediaElement is undefined the controller card is hidden but the event log remains, telling the user to 'interact with the <usermedia> element above' — an element that is no longer on screen. Hide the log alongside the card, or replace its empty-state copy in the unsupported branch.

openQuestions.title: Reconcile the event vocabulary across the usermedia concepts
openQuestions.detail: This page wires onstreamready/userchangedenabled while the event-sequence concept card on the feature index describes an activate event carrying the stream. Both cannot match the explainer. Re-read WICG/PEPC usermedia_element.md, confirm the shipped event names in Chromium source, and align every concept (and the feature blurb) on the real vocabulary.

openQuestions.title: Flag vacuous conformance assertion streamready-event-attribute for human review
openQuestions.detail: The assertion creates an element, setAttribute('onstreamready',''), then checks hasAttribute — which is true for any attribute on any element in any browser, so it can never fail. It should instead probe the IDL event-handler slot (e.g. 'onstreamready' in element). Conformance suites are immutable; a human must decide whether to supersede it with a corrected additive assertion.

openQuestions.title: Announce stream state changes via a live region
openQuestions.detail: Add aria-live=polite to the event log body (or a visually-hidden status element mirroring the controller title) so streamready, mute toggles and stream stop are perceivable without vision. Currently the only text change is visual.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate mid-session track-ended recovery
openQuestions.detail: The sibling camera-permission-flow concept covers track-ended recovery, but this controller — the page a developer would copy for a real capture UI — silently keeps 'Stream active' if the user revokes permission or unplugs the device. Listen for track.onended and surface a recovery path or at least log the event.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot and served-DOM inspection of /v149/capability-elements-usermedia-mvp/stream-controller/ plus the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200, panel rendered 4 pass / 2 fail / 0 blocked). HTMLUserMediaElement is absent in Chromium 141, so only the unsupported fallback path could be exercised — the element click, stream preview, mute and stop controls were not driven. The fallback itself is clean (notice shown, card hidden, no blank stage), but the banner's 'Chrome 149' claim is stale against the recorded Chrome 151 ship, the event log orphans itself in the unsupported branch, and one conformance assertion is vacuous.
